"\nSaves original, silent DNG frames as a ZIP in Download / 5igna1. Regular video players cannot play it directly. Extract the ZIP and develop the frames in RAW-compatible software. Effects and LIVE FAULT are not applied."

RAW processing changes sensor rows, pixels and bits. Its preview is an approximation. Open DNG files in RAW-compatible software.

Standard and RAW videos split into files at about 3.5 GB. Recording stops when storage is low. RAW fps is a target, not a guarantee. Dropped frames and timestamps are recorded inside the ZIP. Keep the app in the foreground while recording."

5igna1 turns camera images into deliberate digital faults. Start with a photo, then shape the damage. This guide is always available in Settings.

Choose PHOTO or VIDEO, then tap the large capture button. Tap again to stop a video. Use the format label to choose JPG or RAW; available formats depend on your camera. Light, location and recording audio are controlled at the top.

Tap + below the preview to select and combine faults. Tap a selected fault to adjust its controls. Apply keeps editor changes; Back discards them. The LEVEL slider changes overall strength immediately. The shuffle icon tries a new random chain.

Enable LIVE for variation over time and reactions to enabled inputs such as motion and sound. PAUSE freezes the variation; TRIGGER triggers a burst. Microphone access is requested when audio reaction needs it. RAW previews are approximations of the saved result.

Tap the thumbnail to open saved photos and videos. Swipe left or right to browse, pinch photos to zoom, and use playback controls for video. Swipe down to return to the camera. Settings also contains this guide, capture options and language.

Follow the highlighted controls to practice without changing settings or saving media. The camera and video icons choose capture mode. In landscape, the viewfinder sits on the left and controls on the right.

Use ＋ to add faults in signal-processing order. Tap a selected fault to edit it; Apply keeps changes and Back discards them. MEDIA and DISPLAY each offer different models. SEED fixes the identity; RESEED changes it while keeping controls. Tap shuffle for a new chain, or hold it to reseed the chain.

LEVEL changes overall strength immediately. Drag this practice slider to compare. Hold the camera or video icon to choose resolution. RAW previews approximate the supported sensor effects; RGB-only effects do not process RAW samples.

LIVE controls fault timing and variation. The adjacent sliders icon opens its settings. PAUSE holds fault evolution, TRIGGER produces a burst and RESET restarts fault time. The camera keeps moving. Some faults have their own motion even with LIVE off; device reactions require their inputs to be enabled.

Tap the format label between capture mode and LIVE to cycle JPG ↔ RAW on supported cameras. Video stays MP4 unless RAW video switching is enabled in Settings; supported cameras can then cycle MP4 ↔ RAW ZIP. RAW video saves original DNG frames without audio. Try the format button below.

Tap the shutter to take a photo or to start and stop video recording. Leaving the app stops recording and saves it. With Experimental features enabled, TAP imports an image or video for downstream faults; it exports JPG or MP4. The guide only changes the practice signal.

The thumbnail opens saved captures. Swipe sideways to browse, pinch photos to zoom and use playback controls for video. Swipe down to return. The light, location and audio controls sit at the top, on the right in landscape.

The gear opens Settings; changes save immediately. Enable RAW video here before switching to RAW ZIP. Experimental features expose TAP and device responses; ADVANCED MODE exposes detailed fault parameters. Use recommended resolution for adaptive load control. Replay this guide from Settings.
Enables additional device responses, TIME ECHO and the TAP media-input tab. OFF preserves adjustments and bypasses these additions.
LIVE must be ON. 0 disconnects this input; 1 is standard; up to 4 amplifies it. AUTO restores the existing route (0 for unused sources). Global input switches and permissions still apply.
Experimental image artifacts simulate normal capture limitations, separately from hardware faults. Temperature is a device proxy, not measured sensor temperature.
Motion-dependent blur using gyro/acceleration and available exposure metadata. A bounded artistic approximation, not optical reconstruction.
Grain driven by device temperature and exposure proxies. This does not measure the image sensor temperature.
Highlight trails along columns, driven by available readout timing. A smear-like simulation, not a claim that this sensor has CCD smear.

Lowers AAC recording quality with video resolution. QVGA: 8 kHz / 24 kbps; VGA: 16 kHz / 48 kbps; HD: 32 kHz / 64 kbps; Full HD: 48 kHz / 128 kbps; higher: 48 kHz / 192 kbps. Device support may adjust these values. Requires audio ON; does not affect RAW video.
Past images interrupt at random. Probability controls automatic events; ECHO triggers one manually. Current FAULT continues. Enable LIVE to use it.
